items.q: A 28-year-old woman undergoes evaluation for three consecutive first-trimester pregnancy losses. Three-dimensional ultrasound demonstrates a normal convex outer fundal uterine contour with an internal muscular partition dividing the cavity into two symmetric halves. What is the most appropriate management for this condition?
items.exp: A septate uterus is characterized by a normal external fundal contour combined with an internal dividing septum due to failure of midline resorption. It is the Müllerian anomaly most strongly associated with recurrent miscarriage. Treatment of choice is hysteroscopic septum resection (metroplasty). Strassman metroplasty is reserved for bicornuate uteri.
r: Correct. Hysteroscopic resection restores normal cavity architecture and significantly reduces miscarriage rates.
Incorrect. Strassman abdominal metroplasty is indicated for bicornuate uterus with fundal clefting, not septate uterus.
Incorrect. Cerclage treats cervical insufficiency, not avascular cavity septal implantation failure.
Incorrect. Progesterone supplementation does not correct the anatomic mechanical and vascular defect.
items.kp: Septate uterus has a normal outer fundal contour and carries the highest rate of recurrent pregnancy loss, treated with hysteroscopic metroplasty.

items.q: During a total abdominal hysterectomy, at which specific anatomical location is the ureter most vulnerable to accidental clamping and ligation?
o: As it passes under the uterine artery within the cardinal ligament
As it crosses the external iliac vein in the obturator fossa
At the level of the renal pelvis beneath the costal margin
Within the broad ligament anterior to the round ligament
items.exp: The ureter is most commonly injured where it passes under the uterine artery within the cardinal (Mackenrodt) ligament, approximately 1.5 to 2.0 cm lateral to the supravaginal cervix (water under the bridge). Other hazard points include the infundibulopelvic ligament and the bladder reflection.
r: Correct. The uterine artery crosses superior to the ureter in the cardinal ligament, making this the most frequent injury site.
Incorrect. The ureter crosses the iliac artery bifurcation, not the obturator fossa.
Incorrect. The renal pelvis is far superior to the pelvis and unaffected by hysterectomy.
Incorrect. The ureter lies in the retroperitoneum, not anterior to the round ligament.
items.kp: The ureter runs beneath the uterine artery within the cardinal ligament, 1.5 to 2 cm lateral to the cervix, the most frequent site of surgical injury.

items.q: How many muscles converge to form the central tendinous point of the perineum (perineal body)?
items.exp: Ten muscles converge at the perineal body: two unpaired muscles (external anal sphincter and longitudinal muscle of the rectum) and four paired muscles (superficial transverse perineal, deep transverse perineal, bulbospongiosus, and levator ani medial slips).
r: Correct. Ten muscles converge on the central tendon: two unpaired plus four pairs of bilateral muscles.
Incorrect. Six accounts only for three paired muscles without rectal and sphincter contributions.
Incorrect. Four muscles underestimate the superficial and deep contributions.
Incorrect. Twelve exceeds the anatomical attachments.
items.kp: The perineal body is formed by the convergence of ten muscles: two unpaired and four paired structures.

items.q: Which ligament provides the principal apical suspensory support to the uterus and vaginal vault, preventing apical descent?
items.exp: The cardinal (Mackenrodt) ligament, together with the uterosacral ligament, provides primary Level I apical support to the cervix and upper vagina. The round ligament maintains uterine anteversion but provides negligible suspensory strength.
r: Correct. Cardinal ligaments provide primary apical structural suspension against pelvic descent.
Incorrect. The round ligament maintains anteversion but provides no suspensory support.
Incorrect. Infundibulopelvic suspensory ligament suspends the ovary and transmits ovarian vessels.
Incorrect. The ovarian ligament connects the ovary to the uterine cornua.
items.kp: Cardinal and uterosacral ligaments provide primary Level I apical support preventing uterine and vault prolapse.

items.q: A 16-year-old girl presents with cyclical monthly lower abdominal pain and primary amenorrhoea. Pelvic examination demonstrates a bluish, tense, bulging membrane at the introitus. What is the diagnosis?
o: Transverse vaginal septum in upper third
items.exp: Cyclical monthly pelvic pain without menstruation in an adolescent with normal secondary sexual characteristics and a tense, bluish, bulging membrane at the introitus is diagnostic of imperforate hymen with hematocolpos. Treatment is cruciate hymenotomy.
r: Correct. Imperforate hymen leads to hematocolpos, presenting as a bluish bulging membrane at the introitus.
Incorrect. CAIS presents with absent pubic hair, inguinal masses, and no hematocolpos.
Incorrect. MRKH syndrome features congenital absence of uterus and upper vagina with no hematocolpos.
Incorrect. High transverse vaginal septum does not present as a bulging membrane at the introitus.
items.kp: Imperforate hymen presents with cyclical abdominal pain, primary amenorrhoea, and a tense bluish bulging introital mass.

items.q: Remnants of the embryonic mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in females may form cystic dilatations along the anterolateral vaginal wall. What is this clinical entity?
items.exp: Gartner duct cysts arise from persistent embryonic mesonephric (Wolffian) duct remnants located along the anterolateral wall of the vagina. Bartholin cysts occur in the posterolateral introitus, while Nabothian cysts are retention cysts of the cervix.
r: Correct. Gartner duct cysts originate from remnants of the Wolffian duct along the anterolateral vaginal wall.
Incorrect. Bartholin gland cysts are situated in the posterior third of the labia majora/introitus.
Incorrect. Nabothian cysts are non-neoplastic mucous retention cysts on the ectocervix.
Incorrect. Skene gland cysts are located adjacent to the external urethral meatus.
items.kp: Gartner duct cysts arise from Wolffian mesonephric remnants in the anterolateral vaginal wall.

items.q: Which arterial branch directly supplies the lower pole of the ovary and anastomoses extensively with the ovarian artery within the mesovarium?
o: Tubal and ovarian branches of the uterine artery
items.exp: The uterine artery terminates by ascending along the lateral uterine margin and branching into fundal, tubal, and ovarian branches. The ovarian branch anastomoses extensively with the ovarian artery (from the abdominal aorta) within the mesovarium, providing dual blood supply.
r: Correct. The uterine artery provides an ovarian branch that forms a robust collateral arcade with the ovarian artery.
Incorrect. Internal pudendal artery supplies the perineum and external genitalia.
Incorrect. Inferior epigastric artery supplies the rectus abdominis muscle.
Incorrect. Middle rectal artery supplies the rectum.
items.kp: The ovary receives dual arterial perfusion via the ovarian artery (aorta) and the ovarian branch of the uterine artery.

items.q: Which structure runs through the inguinal canal in women, entering the labium majus and helping maintain uterine anteversion?
items.exp: The round ligament originates from the uterine cornua, traverses the deep inguinal ring, traverses the inguinal canal, and inserts into the subcutaneous tissue of the labium majus. It assists in maintaining uterine anteversion.
r: Correct. The round ligament courses through the inguinal canal and terminates in the labia majora.
Incorrect. Uterosacral ligament connects the cervix to the second and third sacral vertebrae.
Incorrect. Suspensory ligament of ovary courses in the retroperitoneum towards the infundibulum.
Incorrect. Transverse cervical (cardinal) ligament attaches horizontally to the lateral pelvic sidewall.
items.kp: The round ligament originates at the uterine cornu, traverses the inguinal canal, and inserts into the labium majus.

items.q: An 18-year-old female presents with primary amenorrhoea. Physical examination shows normal secondary sexual characteristics including normal breast development and female pubic hair. Pelvic ultrasound reveals absent uterus and ovaries with normal bilateral follicular morphology. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome is characterized by Müllerian agenesis (46,XX) leading to congenital absence of the uterus, cervix, and upper vagina, accompanied by normal ovarian function and normal secondary sexual characteristics (including female pubic hair). CAIS patients have absent or sparse pubic hair and testicles.
r: Correct. MRKH syndrome is 46,XX Müllerian agenesis with normal ovaries and normal female pubic hair distribution.
Incorrect. CAIS is 46,XY with absent or sparse pubic hair and intra-abdominal testes, not normal ovaries.
Incorrect. Turner syndrome presents with streak ovaries and lack of breast development.
Incorrect. Swyer syndrome presents with streak gonads and lack of spontaneous thelarche.
items.kp: MRKH syndrome is congenital Müllerian agenesis (46,XX) with normal ovaries, normal thelarche, and normal female pubic hair.

items.q: What is the primary histological lining of the endocervical canal?
o: Single layer of tall columnar mucin-secreting epithelium
items.exp: The endocervical canal is lined by a single layer of tall columnar mucin-secreting epithelial cells, which form complex branched crypts. The ectocervix is covered by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium. The squamocolumnar junction forms the transformation zone.
r: Correct. The endocervical mucosa consists of a single layer of tall mucin-secreting columnar cells.
Incorrect. Non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium covers the ectocervix and vagina.
Incorrect. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium lines the respiratory tract.
Incorrect. Transitional epithelium lines the urinary bladder and ureters.
items.kp: The endocervix is lined by tall mucin-secreting columnar epithelium, meeting ectocervical squamous epithelium at the transformation zone.
